QUICK READ / HYBRID & ADAPTABLE WORK

Designing a hybrid workplace.

Plan around the patterns, not the label.

Three ideas to take into your workplace conversation.

01 / 03

Understand attendance over time

Look beyond average attendance to days when teams overlap, visitors arrive or projects bring people together. Shared seats need an operating plan as well as a furniture plan.

Next idea ↓
02 / 03

Support the reason to be there

Decide which activities benefit from being together and which need concentration or privacy. Give those activities appropriate settings instead of making the whole office uniformly collaborative.

Next idea ↓
03 / 03

Make change easy to manage

Movable furniture, shared storage and clear room-use conventions can help. Assign responsibility for reset and upkeep so flexibility does not become daily uncertainty.

Put it in your brief ↗
A PRACTICAL TAKEAWAY

Before you decide.

  • Map peak and typical attendance separately.
  • Test a shared-seat day from arrival to departure.
  • Agree storage and reset conventions.
